```{r}
#| include: false
library(knitr)
d <- readRDS("rds/clean.rds")
tab1 <- readRDS("rds/table1.rds")
tab2 <- readRDS("rds/table2.rds")
```

The report does no computing of its own. It reads the objects the pipeline
produced and displays them, so that rendering it can never quietly change a
result.

## Analysis set

`r nrow(d)` participants had a week 12 measurement:
`r sum(d$arm == "Placebo")` on placebo and
`r sum(d$arm == "Treatment")` on treatment.

## Table 1: baseline characteristics

```{r}
kable(tab1, col.names = c("Characteristic",
                          sprintf("Placebo (n = %d)", attr(tab1, "n")[["Placebo"]]),
                          sprintf("Treatment (n = %d)", attr(tab1, "n")[["Treatment"]])),
      align = "lcc")
```

## Change in FEV1

![](out/figure1.png)

## Table 2: treatment effect

```{r}
kable(tab2, col.names = c("Model", "Effect (95% CI)", "p", "n"), align = "lccc")
```

The estimated treatment effect is `r attr(tab2, "headline")` L in the adjusted
model, and is insensitive to which covariates are included.
